Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR BLEACHING EARTHS OF INDIAN ORIGIN USED FOR BLEACHING VEGETABLE OILS

( First Revision )
0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standarc!s Institution on 24 March 1972, after the draft finalized by the Oils and Oilsecds Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Di\Tision Council and the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 Bleaching earths are used mainly for bleaching oils and fats. In India, thry are used chiefly in the manufacture of edible oil products, such as refined oils, VAJ\rI1SPAT1 and margarine and are also employed for treatment of fatty raw materials in the manufacture of such products as soaps, toilet preparations and paints. 0.3 The two main classes of bleaching earths encountered in commerce are neutral or acidic. Formerly, bleaching earths were notsubjected to special chemical treatment before use but the improved performance of earths which have been activated with acids or other chemicals has led to their predominant use in many fields. 0.4 Formerly, all the bleaching earths~used in this country were imported principally from Britain and Germany. Indigenous production of bleaching earths is now firmly established but certain grades, especially suited for dark-coloured oils that are difficult to bleach, are still being imported though in very small quantities. 0.5 Types and grades of bleaching earths are normally chosen to suit the This applies to imported kind of oil being treated and the result required, The Sectional Committee earths as well those manufactured indigenously. has based this~revised standard on the experience of manufacturers, consumers and testing authorities concerned in the country, as also the valuable data supplied by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research and its laboratories. It is hoped that the specifications prescribed in this revised standard will enable the producers as well as the consumers to have a proper appreciation of the material and will also serve as an incentive to the indigenous industry. 3

-Is : 1965- 1972 6.6 In the revision of the standard, originaIIy pubIished in 1961, the requirement for decolorizing power has been substituted by that for bleaching efficiency, in line with the corresponding change in the standard on the methods of test. The title of the standard has also betin accordingly mddified . 0.7 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with The number of significant piaces retained in the rounded ofY IS : 2-1960*. value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.
